speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower for wrongful dismissal claims lodged with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) since April 2019 (a) how many mediation requests have been refused by TADM; (b) what is the proportion of these requests which have been refused; (c) what are the typical reasons for such refusal; (d) whether TADM mediators assess and advise disputants on the validity of their claims; (e) if so, what laws empower them to do so; and (f) what qualifications are TADM mediators required to have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They must then undergo mediation at the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The intention is for mediation to be the first line of response, failing which claims can be adjudicated at the Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: While such claims are no longer eligible for mediation under the ECA, TADM still assists both parties to resolve the disputes if they were prepared to settle the matter amicably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Usually, this is because the facts as reported by the claimant showed that the employer had contractually terminated the employment in accordance with the Employment Act or the employment contract, and the employee could not cite any other facts suggesting that the termination was wrongful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Some claimants withdraw their case at this stage, after hearing TADM's assessment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: TADM's approach of referring cases to ECT without mediation reduces potential burden on employers, who should not have to attend mediation for unsubstantiated claims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It also does not affect claimants' rights in any way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The outcomes at the ECT generally validate our mediators' assessment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: A large majority of the cases were either dismissed by the Magistrate or withdrawn by the claimants at the ECT – an indication that the process is working well as intended.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Many of TADM's mediators have prior HR experience from varied sectors or were previously employed in the former Labour Court.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: TADM mediators also participate in continuing education, including studying and learning from the grounds of decisions issued by the ECT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This fosters a culture of continuous learning and ensures continuous alignment with the Courts in facilitating a fair outcome for both claimants and respondents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I believe the Senior Minister of State said 6% of the wrongful dismissal claims that go into TADM had lapsed because they do not meet the time bar and 12% are referred to ECT.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Of the remaining 82%, I am just wondering how many are actually dropped due to lack of evidence and how many are actually successful, whereby TADM upholds that there had been wrongful dismissals?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just wondering if I could have that statistic.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My second question is to ask the Senior Minister of State if he could characterise what the lack of evidence issue really is in most cases.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is it a lack of, for example, written email or audio-graphic or video-graphic evidence?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is that usually the reason why the cases cannot be moved forward?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Once they exceed the time bar, then, it is up to the parties to see if they want to proceed with some mediation by TADM, on a voluntary basis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: TADM is prepared to assist them if they are both willing to still have a conversation to resolve the issue amicably.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is probably going to be a biased tracking anyway, for those who are prepared to proceed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, the evidence referred to would be documentary proof, it could be email correspondence.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sometimes, they are also unable to cite specific incidences in which they believe that they are wrongfully dismissed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These are the kinds of things that the TADM team look at when it assesses the ground for dismissal.
